#### C++ `Library` memory/lifetime in Python
The `Library` façade holds `self._core` for its lifetime. Returned `core.Book` references are converted immediately. In `borrow`, we do `book = self._core.find_book(isbn)`, then call `check_out_book`, then `return self.find_book(isbn)`. We must not use the old `book` reference after removal (we don't). In `return_book`, same. In `remove_book`, we read `core_book` fields before remove, then remove. Fine.
If `find_book` is bound with `reference_internal`, the returned object holds a keep-alive to the library; after `remove_book`, using it would dangle. Adapter should copy fields before removal. Plan note.

Alternatively bind `find_book` with `return_value_policy::copy`, eliminating dangling issues. Since adapter only reads, copy is safer. For `all_books`/`all_users`, return copies too. Then no lifetime concerns. `Library.add_book` copies. `check_out` methods on copies wouldn't affect core, but adapter never does that. So bind all getters returning copies:
- `find_book` lambda `-> Book*` with `py::return_value_policy::copy`. Or `std::optional<Book>`? pybind11 supports `std::optional` with C++17 and `<pybind11/stl.h>`; returning `std::optional<Book>` is clean:
  ```cpp
  .def("find_book", [](const Library& lib, const std::string& isbn) -> std::optional<Book> {
      Book* b = const_cast<Library&>(lib).findBookByISBN(isbn);
      if (!b) return std::nullopt;
      return *b;
  })
  ```
  But `findBookByISBN` is non-const; use a non-const lambda `Library&`. Return `std::optional<Book>` (copy). Python gets `Book | None`. `std::optional` caster requires `<pybind11/stl.h>`. Good.
- `all_books` lambda returns `std::vector<Book>` copies:
  ```cpp
  .def("all_books", [](Library& lib) {
      std::vector<Book> result;
      for (Book* b : lib.getAllBooks()) result.push_back(*b);
      return result;
  })
  ```
  `<pybind11/stl.h>` converts to list. Safe.
- `all_users` similarly returns `std::vector<User>`.
- `search_by_title/author` could return `std::vector<Book>` copies, but we may not expose if search stays Python. Could still expose for completeness.
- `find_user` returns `std::optional<User>` copy.

This is a clean, Python-friendly binding API. Then `Book`/`User` in C++ are value types exposed with properties; no lifetime issues.

For mutating operations, adapter calls `Library` methods by ISBN/user ID. Good.

Would returning copies be considered "not really interfacing"? No, it's safe.

"""Tests du modèle de bibliothèque."""

import pytest

from app.models.book import Book
from app.models.library import Library, LibraryError, LibraryStats
from app.models.user import User


def make_library() -> Library:
    return Library(
        books=[
            Book("Le Petit Prince", "Antoine de Saint-Exupéry", "9782070612758"),
            Book("L'Étranger", "Albert Camus", "9782070360024"),
            Book(
                "Les Misérables",
                "Victor Hugo",
                "9782253096337",
                available=False,
                borrower_id="USR001",
            ),
        ],
        users=[
            User("Marie Dubois", "USR001", ["9782253096337"]),
            User("Jean Martin", "USR002"),
        ],
    )


def test_search_ignores_case_and_accents() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    assert [book.isbn for book in library.filtered_books("etranger")] == [
        "9782070360024"
    ]
    assert [book.isbn for book in library.filtered_books("EXUPERY")] == [
        "9782070612758"
    ]
    assert len(library.filtered_books("")) == 3


def test_search_matches_isbn() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    assert [book.isbn for book in library.filtered_books("9782253096337")] == [
        "9782253096337"
    ]


def test_add_book_strips_fields() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    book = library.add_book("  Germinal  ", " Émile Zola ", "9782253004226")

    assert book.title == "Germinal"
    assert book.author == "Émile Zola"
    assert library.find_book("9782253004226") is book


def test_add_book_rejects_duplicate_isbn() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    with pytest.raises(LibraryError, match="existe déjà"):
        library.add_book("Autre titre", "Autre auteur", "9782070612758")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("title", "author", "isbn"),
    [
        ("", "Auteur", "123"),
        ("Titre", "", "123"),
        ("Titre", "Auteur", ""),
        ("Titre|interdit", "Auteur", "123"),
    ],
)
def test_add_book_rejects_invalid_values(
    title: str, author: str, isbn: str
) -> None:
    library = make_library()

    with pytest.raises(LibraryError):
        library.add_book(title, author, isbn)


def test_borrow_book_updates_book_and_user() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    book = library.borrow("9782070612758", "USR002")

    assert book.available is False
    assert book.borrower_id == "USR002"
    assert "9782070612758" in library.find_user("USR002").borrowed_isbns


def test_borrow_unavailable_book_is_rejected() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    with pytest.raises(LibraryError, match="déjà emprunté"):
        library.borrow("9782253096337", "USR002")


def test_borrow_unknown_user_is_rejected() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    with pytest.raises(LibraryError, match="Utilisateur introuvable"):
        library.borrow("9782070612758", "USR999")


def test_return_book_clears_borrower() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    book = library.return_book("9782253096337")

    assert book.available is True
    assert book.borrower_id == ""
    assert "9782253096337" not in library.find_user("USR001").borrowed_isbns


def test_return_available_book_is_rejected() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    with pytest.raises(LibraryError, match="déjà disponible"):
        library.return_book("9782070612758")


def test_remove_book_detaches_it_from_users() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    library.remove_book("9782253096337")

    assert library.find_book("9782253096337") is None
    assert library.find_user("USR001").borrowed_isbns == []


def test_statistics() -> None:
    library = make_library()

    assert library.statistics() == LibraryStats(
        total=3,
        available=2,
        borrowed=1,
        users=2,
    )
=== repository tests ===
"""Tests de la lecture et de l'écriture des données."""

from pathlib import Path

from app.models.book import Book
from app.models.library import Library
from app.models.user import User
from app.repositories.library_repository import LibraryRepository


def write_sample(data_dir: Path) -> None:
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (data_dir / "books.txt").write_text(
        "Le Petit Prince|Antoine de Saint-Exupéry|9782070612758|1|\n"
        "Les Misérables|Victor Hugo|9782253096337|0|USR001\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (data_dir / "users.txt").write_text(
        "Marie Dubois|USR001|9782253096337\n"
        "Jean Martin|USR002|\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


def test_load_reads_books_and_users(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    write_sample(tmp_path)

    library = LibraryRepository(tmp_path).load()

    assert [book.isbn for book in library.books] == [
        "9782070612758",
        "9782253096337",
    ]
    assert library.books[0].title == "Le Petit Prince"
    assert library.books[0].available is True
    assert library.books[1].available is False
    assert library.books[1].borrower_id == "USR001"
    assert library.find_user("USR001").borrowed_isbns == ["9782253096337"]
    assert library.find_user("USR002").borrowed_isbns == []


def test_load_missing_files_returns_empty_library(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    library = LibraryRepository(tmp_path).load()

    assert library.books == []
    assert library.users == []


def test_load_ignores_incomplete_lines(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    (tmp_path / "books.txt").write_text(
        "Titre sans ISBN|Auteur\n"
        "Bon livre|Bon auteur|123|1|\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (tmp_path / "users.txt").write_text(
        "Utilisateur sans identifiant\n"
        "Nom valide|U1|\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    library = LibraryRepository(tmp_path).load()

    assert [book.isbn for book in library.books] == ["123"]
    assert [user.user_id for user in library.users] == ["U1"]


def test_save_round_trip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    library = Library(
        books=[
            Book("Le Petit Prince", "Antoine de Saint-Exupéry", "9782070612758"),
            Book(
                "Les Misérables",
                "Victor Hugo",
                "9782253096337",
                available=False,
                borrower_id="USR001",
            ),
        ],
        users=[
            User("Marie Dubois", "USR001", ["9782253096337"]),
            User("Jean Martin", "USR002"),
        ],
    )
    repository = LibraryRepository(tmp_path)

    repository.save(library)

    assert (tmp_path / "books.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == (
        "Le Petit Prince|Antoine de Saint-Exupéry|9782070612758|1|\n"
        "Les Misérables|Victor Hugo|9782253096337|0|USR001\n"
    )
    assert (tmp_path / "users.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == (
        "Marie Dubois|USR001|9782253096337\n"
        "Jean Martin|USR002|\n"
    )

    reloaded = repository.load()
    assert reloaded.find_book("9782253096337").borrower_id == "USR001"
    assert reloaded.find_user("USR001").borrowed_isbns == ["9782253096337"]


def test_save_creates_missing_directory(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repository = LibraryRepository(tmp_path / "donnees")

    repository.save(Library())

    assert (tmp_path / "donnees" / "books.txt").exists()
    assert (tmp_path / "donnees" / "users.txt").exists()

If we modify `FileManager` to atomic:
```cpp
static bool writeLines(const string& filename, const vector<string>& lines) {
    string temp = filename + ".tmp";
    ofstream file(temp);
    if (!file.is_open()) return false;
    for (auto& line : lines) file << line << "\n";
    file.close();
    if (!file) return false;
    error_code ec;
    filesystem::rename(temp, filename, ec);
    if (ec) { filesystem::remove(temp, ec); return false; }
    return true;
}
```

#### Detach ISBN from users on remove
Order:
```python
core_book = self._core.find_book(isbn)
if core_book is None: raise ...
snapshot = Book(...)
if not self._core.remove_book(isbn): raise ...
for user in self._core.all_users():
    user.return_book(isbn)  # user is a copy!
```
If `all_users` returns copies, `user.return_book` mutates the Python copy, not core. Need a way to remove from core users. Options:
- Bind `Library::removeBook` to a wrapper that also detaches users. Could modify C++ `Library::removeBook` to detach (better, fixes bug) or add a C++ method `detach_isbn_from_users`.
- Or bind `User.return_book` and use `find_user` returning a reference (not copy) to mutate. But our getters return copies.
- Or add a `Library` method in bindings/ C++: `remove_book` wrapper:
  ```cpp
  .def("remove_book", [](Library& lib, const std::string& isbn) {
      bool removed = lib.removeBook(isbn);
      if (removed) {
          for (User* user : lib.getAllUsers()) user->returnBook(isbn);
      }
      return removed;
  })
  ```
  This puts cleanup in bindings, no C++ class change. Good. But then `Library::removeBook` semantics differ from C++ CLI (still bug there). Alternatively modify C++ `Library::removeBook` itself to detach; that fixes both CLI and binding. Which is better? The Python UI previously detached; the C++ CLI should too. I'd modify `Library::removeBook` in C++ to remove the ISBN from all users before/after erasing. That's a small, sensible bug fix. Then binding calls it directly, adapter doesn't need to iterate. Tests `test_remove_book_detaches_it_from_users` pass. This is a C++ change but justified for parity.
  
  Let's examine `Library::removeBook`: it finds the iterator, erases. We can add:
  ```cpp
  if (it != books.end()) {
      for (auto& user : users) user->returnBook(isbn);
      books.erase(it);
      return true;
  }
  ```
  `returnBook` on a user without the ISBN is safe (find then erase if found). Good. Do this before erase or after; both fine. This makes C++ and Python consistent.
  
  Alternatively adapter can use a new binding method `detach_isbn`; but modifying Library is cleaner. Include in plan as "petit correctif de cohérence".

## Principe

Le coeur métier reste le C++ existant (`Book`, `User`, `Library`, `FileManager`). Un module pybind11, `bibliotheque_core`, l'expose à Python. Côté UI, `Library` et `LibraryRepository` deviennent des façades minces sur ce module : le contrôleur, les vues et `main.py` gardent leur API actuelle.

L'objectif est d'avoir une seule source de vérité : l'état de la bibliothèque et la persistance vivent en C++, pas dans une réimplémentation Python.

## Architecture cible

```text
agent/
├── bindings/
│   ├── library_bindings.cpp      # nouveau : module pybind11
│   └── build.sh                  # nouveau : configuration + compilation
├── CMakeLists.txt                # cible bibliotheque_core ajoutée
├── book.cpp/h, user.cpp/h,
│   library.cpp/h, filemanager.cpp/h   # petits correctifs de parité
└── UI/
    ├── app/
    │   ├── bibliotheque_core*.so      # généré, ignoré par Git
    │   ├── models/
    │   │   ├── book.py                # inchangé (dataclass)
    │   │   ├── user.py                # inchangé (dataclass)
    │   │   └── library.py             # façade Python sur le C++
    │   └── repositories/
    │       └── library_repository.py  # utilise FileManager C++
    └── tests/
        ├── test_bindings.py           # nouveau
        ├── test_library.py            # adapté au backend C++
        ├── test_repository.py         # adapté au FileManager C++
        └── test_controller.py         # ajustements légers
```

## Étapes proposées

### 1. Module pybind11

Créer `agent/bindings/library_bindings.cpp` et exposer, en snake_case :

- **`Book`** : constructeurs, propriétés `title`, `author`, `isbn`, `available`, `borrower_id`, méthodes `check_out`, `return_book`, `to_file_format`.
- **`User`** : constructeurs, `name`, `user_id`, `borrowed_isbns` (copie), `borrow_book`, `return_book`, `has_borrowed_book`, `borrowed_count`.
- **`Library`** : `add_book`, `remove_book`, `find_book`, `add_user`, `find_user`, `all_books`, `all_users`, `available_books`, `check_out_book`, `return_book`, `total_books`, `available_count`, `checked_out_count`.
- **`FileManager`** : `load_library`, `save_library`, `load_books`, `save_books`, `load_users`, `save_users`, `file_exists`, `create_backup`.

Les getters renvoient des **copies** (`std::optional<Book>`, `std::vector<Book>`, etc.) pour éviter tout pointeur invalide après suppression ou rechargement. L'adaptateur Python n'a besoin que de lire les objets ; les mutations passent par `Library`.

### 2. Petits correctifs C++ de parité

Ces changements sont nécessaires pour que le comportement de l'UI reste identique :

- `filemanager.cpp` : ignorer les lignes incomplètes au chargement (au moins 4 champs et ISBN non vide pour les livres ; au moins 2 champs et identifiant non vide pour les utilisateurs). Sans cela, le C++ chargerait des livres/utilisateurs vides, contrairement à l'implémentation Python actuelle.
- `library.cpp` : `removeBook` retire aussi l'ISBN des listes d'emprunt des utilisateurs, comme le faisait le modèle Python.
- `library.cpp` : remplacer `::tolower` par un appel sûr avec `unsigned char` dans les recherches, pour éviter un comportement indéfini sur les caractères UTF-8.
- **Option à valider** : rendre l'écriture de `FileManager` atomique (fichier temporaire puis `rename`), pour conserver la garantie de l'implémentation Python actuelle.

### 3. Compilation

Ajouter dans `agent/CMakeLists.txt` une option et une cible :

```cmake
option(BUILD_PYTHON_BINDINGS "Construire le module Python pybind11" OFF)

if(BUILD_PYTHON_BINDINGS)
    find_package(Python REQUIRED COMPONENTS Interpreter Development.Module)
    find_package(pybind11 CONFIG REQUIRED)

    pybind11_add_module(bibliotheque_core
        bindings/library_bindings.cpp
        book.cpp user.cpp library.cpp filemanager.cpp
    )
    target_include_directories(bibliotheque_core PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
    set_target_properties(bibliotheque_core PROPERTIES
        CXX_STANDARD 17
        CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED YES
        LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/UI/app"
    )
endif()
```

Ajouter `pybind11` à `agent/UI/requirements-dev.txt`, puis fournir `agent/bindings/build.sh` qui utilise explicitement le Python du venv :

```bash
cd /workspaces/420-5G4-ML/agent/UI
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
cd ..
./bindings/build.sh
```

Le script configure avec `-DPython_EXECUTABLE=.../UI/.venv/bin/python` et `-Dpybind11_DIR=$(... -m pybind11 --cmakedir)` pour garantir la compatibilité ABI. Le `.so` est produit dans `agent/UI/app/`, donc importable via `from app import bibliotheque_core`.

### 4. Façades Python

- `app/models/library.py` conserve `Library`, `LibraryError`, `LibraryStats`, `normalize` et `filtered_books`, mais délègue l'état et les opérations à `bibliotheque_core`.
- `Library.books` et `Library.users` convertissent les objets C++ en dataclasses `Book` / `User` pour le contrôleur et les tests.
- Les échecs booléens du C++ sont traduits en `LibraryError` avec les messages français actuels.
- `app/repositories/library_repository.py` conserve `load()` / `save()` mais utilise `FileManager`. `save()` crée le dossier si nécessaire et lève `OSError` si le C++ échoue.
- `main.py`, `MainController` et les vues ne changent pas, sauf un message explicite si le module natif est absent.
- L'ancienne implémentation Python de `Library` est supprimée : elle reste accessible dans l'historique Git, mais on évite ainsi deux logiques divergentes.

### 5. Tests

- `test_library.py` : mêmes scénarios, exécutés à travers la façade C++. L'assertion `find_book(...) is book` devient une comparaison de champs, puisque les objets renvoyés sont des copies.
- `test_repository.py` : chargement/sauvegarde via le `FileManager` C++, y compris les lignes incomplètes et la création du dossier de données.
- `test_bindings.py` : tests directs du module (`Book`, `Library`, `FileManager`) pour isoler les erreurs de binding.
- `test_controller.py` : reste globalement inchangé ; il utilise la façade C++ avec les mêmes données de test.
- `test_view_smoke.py` : inchangé.
- Si le module n'est pas compilé, les tests concernés utilisent `pytest.importorskip` avec un message explicite, plutôt qu'une erreur d'import peu lisible.

### 6. Documentation

Mettre à jour `agent/UI/README.md` et `agent/chatLogs/AGENTS.md` avec :

- les prérequis de compilation (`cmake`, `g++`, `pybind11`) ;
- la commande de build du module ;
- le fait que l'UI et les tests nécessitent le module compilé ;
- la nouvelle répartition : C++ pour l'état et la persistance, Python pour la présentation et la recherche accent-insensible.

## Correspondance des opérations

| Opération UI | Avant (Python) | Après |
|---|---|---|
| Chargement | parsing Python | `FileManager::loadLibraryData` |
| Ajout | `Library.add_book` | validation Python + `Library::addBook` |
| Suppression | `Library.remove_book` | `Library::removeBook` + détachement des utilisateurs |
| Emprunt | `Library.borrow` | `Library::checkOutBook` |
| Retour | `Library.return_book` | `Library::returnBook` |
| Statistiques | comptage Python | `getTotalBooks`, `getAvailableBookCount`, `getCheckedOutBookCount` |
| Sauvegarde | écriture atomique Python | `FileManager::saveLibraryData` (+ atomicité C++ si validée) |
| Recherche | filtre Python | filtre Python sur les objets renvoyés par le C++ |

Atomic helper:
```cpp
namespace {

bool writeLinesAtomically(const string& filename, const vector<string>& lines) {
    filesystem::path target(filename);
    filesystem::path temporary = target;
    temporary += ".tmp";

    ofstream file(temporary, ios::out | ios::trunc);
    if (!file.is_open()) {
        return false;
    }

    for (const string& line : lines) {
        file << line << "\n";
    }
    file.flush();
    if (!file.good()) {
        file.close();
        error_code ec;
        filesystem::remove(temporary, ec);
        return false;
    }
    file.close();

    error_code ec;
    filesystem::rename(temporary, target, ec);
    if (ec) {
        filesystem::remove(temporary, ec);
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

bool looksLikeBookLine(const string& line) {
    return count(line.begin(), line.end(), '|') >= 3;
}

bool looksLikeUserLine(const string& line) {
    return count(line.begin(), line.end(), '|') >= 1;
}

}
```

#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <pybind11/pybind11.h>
#include <pybind11/stl.h>

#include "book.h"
#include "filemanager.h"
#include "library.h"
#include "user.h"

namespace py = pybind11;

namespace {

std::vector<Book> copyBooks(const std::vector<Book*>& books) {
    std::vector<Book> copies;
    copies.reserve(books.size());
    for (Book* book : books) {
        copies.push_back(*book);
    }
    return copies;
}

std::vector<User> copyUsers(const std::vector<User*>& users) {
    std::vector<User> copies;
    copies.reserve(users.size());
    for (User* user : users) {
        copies.push_back(*user);
    }
    return copies;
}

} // namespace

PYBIND11_MODULE(bibliotheque_core, module) {
    module.doc() = "Liaison Python du coeur C++ de la bibliotheque personnelle.";

    py::class_<Book>(module, "Book")
        .def(py::init<>())
        .def(py::init<const std::string&, const std::string&, const std::string&>(),
             py::arg("title"), py::arg("author"), py::arg("isbn"))
        .def_property("title", &Book::getTitle, &Book::setTitle)
        .def_property("author", &Book::getAuthor, &Book::setAuthor)
        .def_property("isbn", &Book::getISBN, &Book::setISBN)
        .def_property("available", &Book::getAvailability, &Book::setAvailability)
        .def_property("borrower_id", &Book::getBorrowerId, &Book::setBorrowerId)
        .def("check_out", &Book::checkOut, py::arg("borrower_id"))
        .def("return_book", &Book::returnBook)
        .def("to_file_format", &Book::toFileFormat)
        .def("from_file_format", &Book::fromFileFormat, py::arg("line"));

    py::class_<User>(module, "User")
        .def(py::init<>())
        .def(py::init<const std::string&, const std::string&>(),
             py::arg("name"), py::arg("user_id"))
        .def_property("name", &User::getName, &User::setName)
        .def_property("user_id", &User::getUserId, &User::setUserId)
        .def_property_readonly("borrowed_isbns", &User::getBorrowedBooks)
        .def("borrow_book", &User::borrowBook, py::arg("isbn"))
        .def("return_book", &User::returnBook, py::arg("isbn"))
        .def("has_borrowed_book", &User::hasBorrowedBook, py::arg("isbn"))
        .def("borrowed_count", &User::getNumberOfBorrowedBooks)
        .def("to_file_format", &User::toFileFormat)
        .def("from_file_format", &User::fromFileFormat, py::arg("line"));

    py::class_<Library>(module, "Library")
        .def(py::init<>())
        .def("add_book", &Library::addBook, py::arg("book"))
        .def("remove_book", &Library::removeBook, py::arg("isbn"))
        .def("find_book", [](Library& library, const std::string& isbn) -> std::optional<Book> {
            Book* book = library.findBookByISBN(isbn);
            if (book == nullptr) {
                return std::nullopt;
            }
            return *book;
        }, py::arg("isbn"))
        .def("add_user", &Library::addUser, py::arg("user"))
        .def("find_user", [](Library& library, const std::string& user_id) -> std::optional<User> {
            User* user = library.findUserById(user_id);
            if (user == nullptr) {
                return std::nullopt;
            }
            return *user;
        }, py::arg("user_id"))
        .def("all_books", [](Library& library) {
            return copyBooks(library.getAllBooks());
        })
        .def("all_users", [](Library& library) {
            return copyUsers(library.getAllUsers());
        })
        .def("available_books", [](Library& library) {
            return copyBooks(library.getAvailableBooks());
        })
        .def("search_by_title", [](Library& library, const std::string& title) {
            return copyBooks(library.searchBooksByTitle(title));
        }, py::arg("title"))
        .def("search_by_author", [](Library& library, const std::string& author) {
            return copyBooks(library.searchBooksByAuthor(author));
        }, py::arg("author"))
        .def("check_out_book", &Library::checkOutBook, py::arg("isbn"), py::arg("user_id"))
        .def("return_book", &Library::returnBook, py::arg("isbn"))
        .def("total_books", &Library::getTotalBooks)
        .def("available_count", &Library::getAvailableBookCount)
        .def("checked_out_count", &Library::getCheckedOutBookCount);

    py::class_<FileManager>(module, "FileManager")
        .def(py::init<const std::string&, const std::string&>(),
             py::arg("books_file"), py::arg("users_file"))
        .def("load_library", &FileManager::loadLibraryData, py::arg("library"))
        .def("save_library", &FileManager::saveLibraryData, py::arg("library"))
        .def("load_books", &FileManager::loadBooksFromFile, py::arg("library"))
        .def("save_books", &FileManager::saveBooksToFile, py::arg("library"))
        .def("load_users", &FileManager::loadUsersFromFile, py::arg("library"))
        .def("save_users", &FileManager::saveUsersToFile, py::arg("library"))
        .def("file_exists", &FileManager::fileExists, py::arg("filename"))
        .def("create_backup", &FileManager::createBackup);
}

"""Modèle de la bibliothèque, façade Python sur le coeur C++."""

from __future__ import annotations

import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

try:
    from app import bibliotheque_core as _native
except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - dépend du build natif
    _native = None
    _NATIVE_IMPORT_ERROR = exc
else:
    _NATIVE_IMPORT_ERROR = None

from app.models.book import Book
from app.models.user import User

_FORBIDDEN_CHARACTERS = ("|", "\n", "\r")


class LibraryError(Exception):
    """Erreur métier présentée directement à l'utilisateur."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LibraryStats:
    ...


def require_native() -> Any:
    """Renvoie le module C++ ou explique comment le compiler."""
    if _native is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Le module natif 'bibliotheque_core' est introuvable.\n"
            "Compilez-le depuis agent/ avec : ./bindings/build.sh"
        ) from _NATIVE_IMPORT_ERROR
    return _native


def normalize(text: str) -> str:
    ...


class Library:
    """Collection de livres et d'utilisateurs adossée au C++."""

    def __init__(self, books=None, users=None):
        self._native = require_native()
        self._core = self._native.Library()
        for book in books or []:
            self._core.add_book(self._to_native_book(book))
        for user in users or []:
            self._core.add_user(self._to_native_user(user))

    @property
    def native(self):
        """Objet C++ sous-jacent, réservé au dépôt de données."""
        return self._core

    @property
    def books(self) -> list[Book]:
        return [self._to_book(book) for book in self._core.all_books()]

    @property
    def users(self) -> list[User]:
        return [self._to_user(user) for user in self._core.all_users()]

    def find_book(self, isbn: str) -> Book | None:
        book = self._core.find_book(isbn)
        return None if book is None else self._to_book(book)

    def find_user(self, user_id: str) -> User | None:
        user = self._core.find_user(user_id)
        return None if user is None else self._to_user(user)

    def borrower_name(self, book: Book) -> str | None:
        if not book.borrower_id:
            return None
        user = self.find_user(book.borrower_id)
        return user.name if user else None

    def filtered_books(self, query: str = "") -> list[Book]:
        query = query.strip()
        if not query:
            return self.books
        needle = normalize(query)
        return [
            book
            for book in self.books
            if needle in normalize(book.title)
            or needle in normalize(book.author)
            or needle in normalize(book.isbn)
        ]

    def statistics(self) -> LibraryStats:
        return LibraryStats(
            total=self._core.total_books(),
            available=self._core.available_count(),
            borrowed=self._core.checked_out_count(),
            users=len(self._core.all_users()),
        )

    def add_book(self, title, author, isbn) -> Book:
        title = self._clean_field(title, "Le titre")
        author = self._clean_field(author, "L'auteur")
        isbn = self._clean_field(isbn, "L'ISBN")

        if self._core.find_book(isbn) is not None:
            raise LibraryError(f"Un livre avec l'ISBN {isbn} existe déjà.")

        book = self._native.Book(title, author, isbn)
        self._core.add_book(book)
        return self._to_book(book)

    def remove_book(self, isbn: str) -> Book:
        book = self.find_book(isbn)
        if book is None:
            raise LibraryError("Livre introuvable.")
        if not self._core.remove_book(isbn):
            raise LibraryError("Livre introuvable.")
        return book

    def borrow(self, isbn: str, user_id: str) -> Book:
        book = self._core.find_book(isbn)
        if book is None:
            raise LibraryError("Livre introuvable.")
        if not book.available:
            raise LibraryError("Ce livre est déjà emprunté.")
        if self._core.find_user(user_id) is None:
            raise LibraryError("Utilisateur introuvable.")
        if not self._core.check_out_book(isbn, user_id):
            raise LibraryError("Impossible d'emprunter ce livre.")
        return self.find_book(isbn)  # type: ignore[return-value]

    def return_book(self, isbn: str) -> Book:
        book = self._core.find_book(isbn)
        if book is None:
            raise LibraryError("Livre introuvable.")
        if book.available:
            raise LibraryError("Ce livre est déjà disponible.")
        if not self._core.return_book(isbn):
            raise LibraryError("Impossible de retourner ce livre.")
        return self.find_book(isbn)  # type: ignore[return-value]

    @staticmethod
    def _clean_field(value: str, label: str) -> str:
        ...

    def _to_native_book(self, book: Book):
        native_book = self._native.Book(book.title, book.author, book.isbn)
        native_book.available = book.available
        native_book.borrower_id = book.borrower_id
        return native_book

    def _to_native_user(self, user: User):
        native_user = self._native.User(user.name, user.user_id)
        for isbn in user.borrowed_isbns:
            native_user.borrow_book(isbn)
        return native_user

    @staticmethod
    def _to_book(book) -> Book:
        return Book(
            title=book.title,
            author=book.author,
            isbn=book.isbn,
            available=book.available,
            borrower_id=book.borrower_id,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _to_user(user) -> User:
        return User(
            name=user.name,
            user_id=user.user_id,
            borrowed_isbns=list(user.borrowed_isbns),
        )

```python
"""Lecture et écriture des fichiers de données de la bibliothèque."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from app.models.library import Library, require_native


class LibraryRepository:
    """Accès aux fichiers books.txt et users.txt via le FileManager C++."""

    def __init__(self, data_dir: Path | str) -> None:
        native = require_native()
        self.data_dir = Path(data_dir)
        self.books_path = self.data_dir / "books.txt"
        self.users_path = self.data_dir / "users.txt"
        self._file_manager = native.FileManager(
            str(self.books_path),
            str(self.users_path),
        )

    def load(self) -> Library:
        """Charge les livres et les utilisateurs, ou renvoie une bibliothèque vide."""
        library = Library()
        # False signifie ici "aucun fichier trouvé", pas une erreur.
        self._file_manager.load_library(library.native)
        return library

    def save(self, library: Library) -> None:
        """Écrit les deux fichiers de façon atomique via le C++."""
        self.data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            saved = self._file_manager.save_library(library.native)
        except Exception as error:  # pragma: no cover - dépend du système
            raise OSError(
                "Impossible d'enregistrer les données de la bibliothèque."
            ) from error
        if not saved:
            raise OSError(
                "Impossible d'enregistrer les données de la bibliothèque."
            )
```

{
  "content": "# Interface graphique (Python / customtkinter)\n\nInterface de gestion de la bibliothèque personnelle, construite en MVC avec\ncustomtkinter. La mise en page reprend `agent/maquetteUI.png` : barre latérale,\nen-tête avec recherche, tableau des livres et actions en bas à droite.\n\nLe coeur métier et la persistance sont assurés par le code C++ du projet,\nexposé à Python avec **pybind11**. La couche Python ne contient que la\nprésentation, la navigation et la recherche accent-insensible.\n\n## Prérequis\n\n- Python 3.13 avec Tkinter.\n- Un compilateur C++17 et CMake (3.21 ou plus).\n- Un serveur d'affichage X11 ou Wayland. Le devcontainer transmet déjà\n  `DISPLAY` depuis l'hôte.\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\ncd agent/UI\npython3 -m venv .venv\n.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt\n```\n\nLe venv est dédié à l'interface et ignoré par Git. Il est distinct du venv\nutilisé par les notebooks à la racine du dépôt.\n\n## Compilation du module natif\n\nLe module `bibliotheque_core` doit être compilé avant de lancer l'interface :\n\n```bash\ncd agent\n./bindings/build.sh\n```\n\nLe script utilise le Python de `UI/.venv`, configure CMake avec pybind11 et\nécrit le module dans `UI/app/`. Il est possible de faire la même chose à la\nmain :\n\n```bash\ncd agent\ncmake -S . -B build-pybind11 \\\n    -DBUILD_PYTHON_BINDINGS=ON \\\n    -DPython_EXECUTABLE=\"$PWD/UI/.venv/bin/python\" \\\n    -Dpybind11_DIR=\"$(\"$PWD/UI/.venv/bin/python\" -m pybind11 --cmakedir)\"\ncmake --build build-pybind11 --target bibliotheque_core -j\n```\n\nLe module compilé est ignoré par Git. Après une modification du C++, relancer\n`./bindings/build.sh`.\n\n## Lancement\n\n```bash\ncd agent/UI\n.venv/bin/python main.py\n```\n\nSi le module natif est absent, l'application s'arrête avec un message\nindiquant la commande de compilation à exécuter.\n\n## Données\n\nL'application lit au démarrage les fichiers du dossier `agent/data/` avec le\n`FileManager` C++ :\n\n- `books.txt` : `titre|auteur|isbn|disponible|idEmprunteur` ;\n- `users.txt` : `nom|identifiant|isbn1,isbn2`.\n\nLes actions **Ajouter**, **Emprunter**, **Retourner** et **Supprimer**\nréécrivent ces deux fichiers au même format que le programme C++. L'écriture\nse fait dans un fichier temporaire renommé ensuite, afin de ne pas laisser un\nfichier tronqué en cas d'erreur. Pour revenir aux données d'origine :\n\n```bash\ngit checkout -- agent/data\n```\n\n## Fonctionnalités\n\n- **Recherche** en direct par titre, auteur ou ISBN, insensible aux accents et\n  à la casse.\n- **Tableau** des livres avec statut Disponible / Emprunté, sélection au clic\n  et mise en évidence de la ligne.\n- **Ajouter** un livre via une fenêtre modale (validation des champs et\n  unicité de l'ISBN).\n- **Emprunter** un livre disponible en choisissant l'utilisateur dans une\n  liste ; le même bouton devient **Retourner** pour un livre emprunté.\n- **Supprimer** le livre sélectionné après confirmation.\n- **Navigation** : Livres est fonctionnel ; Utilisateurs, Emprunts et\n  Statistiques affichent une section « à venir ».\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\ncd agent/UI\n.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q\n```\n\nLes tests du modèle et du dépôt utilisent le module natif ; ils sont ignorés\navec un message explicite s'il n'a pas été compilé. Le test de fumée de la\nfenêtre nécessite un affichage et est ignoré automatiquement s'il n'y en a pas :\n\n```bash\nxvfb-run -a .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q\n```\n\n## Structure MVC\n\n```text\nagent/\n├── bindings/\n│   ├── library_bindings.cpp             # module pybind11\n│   └── build.sh                         # compilation du module\n├── book.cpp/h, user.cpp/h\n├── library.cpp/h, filemanager.cpp/h     # coeur C++ et persistance\n└── UI/\n    ├── main.py                          # composition root\n    ├── app/\n    │   ├── config.py                    # dimensions, palette, libellés\n    │   ├── bibliotheque_core*.so        # module généré, ignoré\n    │   ├── models/\n    │   │   ├── book.py                  # dataclass Book\n    │   │   ├── user.py                  # dataclass User\n    │   │   └── library.py               # façade Python sur le C++\n    │   ├── repositories/\n    │   │   └── library_repository.py    # FileManager C++\n    │   ├── views/\n    │   │   ├── main_window.py           # fenêtre, sidebar, en-tête, pied\n    │   │   ├── book_table.py            # tableau scrollable\n    │   │   ├── dialogs.py               # ajout et choix d'utilisateur\n    │   │   └── view_models.py           # BookRow / UserRow\n    │   └── controllers/\n    │       └── main_controller.py       # câblage vue ↔ modèle ↔ dépôt\n    └── tests/\n        ├── test_bindings.py\n        ├── test_library.py\n        ├── test_repository.py\n        ├── test_controller.py\n        └── test_view_smoke.py\n```\n\nRègles de dépendance :\n\n- l'état des livres et des utilisateurs vit dans le C++ ; la façade Python ne\n  fait que convertir et valider les entrées ;\n- la vue n'importe pas le modèle ; elle reçoit des `BookRow` / `UserRow`\n  prêts à afficher ;\n- le contrôleur ne crée aucun widget ;\n- le dépôt centralise les accès aux fichiers via le `FileManager` C++ ;\n- seul `main.py` connaît les trois couches à la fois.\n",
  "path": "/workspaces/420-5G4-ML/agent/UI/README.md"
}

3: ## Repository shape
4: - Three independent ateliers; there is no root build, test, lint, or CI entrypoint.

6:   - `analyse_image/`: TensorFlow/Keras notebooks (Fashion-MNIST CNN).
7:   - `agent/`: C++17 CLI `bibliotheque` (CMake), the only compiled project; it
8:     also contains the Python/customtkinter UI under `agent/UI/`.

11: ## Python notebooks
12: - Use the local venv: `.venv/bin/python` (currently Python 3.13.5; check with `.venv/bin/python --version`). It is git-ignored and there is no `requirements.txt`/lockfile.
13: - The venv has `ipykernel` but no JupyterLab/Notebook server; use VS Code's notebook UI.
14: - Notebooks use relative `datas/` and `modele/` paths. Run them with the notebook's own directory as cwd; running from the repo root breaks every path.
15: - `analyse_image`: run `classification.ipynb` before `test_model.ipynb`; the former writes `modele/modele.json` and `modele/modele.weights.h5`.
16: - `apprentissage`: `partie1_2.ipynb` writes `datas/dataset.csv` (tab-separated); `partie3_entrainement.ipynb` reads it and writes `modele/modele_pokemon.mod`; `partie3_predictions.ipynb` loads that model.
17: - `analyse_image/datas/.gitignore` ignores `*`: Fashion-MNIST CSVs/IDX files exist only locally. `apprentissage/datas/*` is tracked.
18: 
19: ## C++ (`agent/`)
20: - CMake is not installed on the host; `g++`/`make` are. Build inside `agent/.devcontainer` (CMake 3.22.2, X11 forwarding). The devcontainer config is under `agent/`, not the repo root.
21: - Fresh build:
22:   ```
23:   cd agent
24:   rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build
25:   cmake .. && make
26:   ```
27: - The existing `agent/build/` cache was generated in the devcontainer (`/workspaces/420-5G4-ML/agent`) and is not reusable on the host. Delete it if CMake reports a source-directory mismatch. `build/` is git-ignored.
28: - `CMakeLists.txt` uses `file(GLOB *.cpp)`: re-run `cmake ..` after adding/removing a source file; `make` alone will not notice it.
29: - Run from `agent/`: `./build/bibliotheque -d data`. Without `-d`, data file paths are empty and load/save fail.
30: - Persistence formats: `books.txt` = `title|author|isbn|1|borrowerId`; `users.txt` = `name|userId|isbn1,isbn2`.
31: 
32: ## Python UI (`agent/UI/`)
33: - Dedicated venv: `agent/UI/.venv` (git-ignored). Do not reuse the root notebook venv.
34: - Setup: `cd agent/UI && python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`
35: - Run: `cd agent/UI && .venv/bin/python main.py`. Requires an X display (`DISPLAY` is forwarded by the devcontainer).
36: - Tests: `cd agent/UI && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`. GUI smoke tests need a display; use `xvfb-run -a` when `DISPLAY` is unset.
37: - MVC layout: `app/models` holds `Book`/`User`/`Library` with no Tk imports; `app/repositories` reads/writes `agent/data`; `app/views` contains only CTk widgets and receives `BookRow`/`UserRow`; `app/controllers` wires everything; `main.py` is the composition root.
38: - Data: `agent/data/books.txt` (`titre|auteur|isbn|1|` or `0|USRxxx`) and `users.txt` (`nom|id|isbn1,isbn2`). The UI reads at launch and rewrites both files after add/borrow/return/delete; restore with `git checkout -- agent/data`.
39: - Screen: sidebar Livres/Utilisateurs/Emprunts/Statistiques (only Livres is active), accent-insensitive search by title/author/ISBN, book table, and Ajouter / Emprunter↔Retourner / Supprimer.
40: - UI text and comments are French; identifiers are English.

#include <cctype>
#include <iostream>
#include <algorithm>

#include "library.h"

using namespace std;

// Constructor
Library::Library() {}

// Add book to library
void Library::addBook(const Book& book) {
    books.push_back(make_unique<Book>(book));
}

// Remove book from library
bool Library::removeBook(const string& isbn) {
    auto it = find_if(books.begin(), books.end(),
        [&isbn](const unique_ptr<Book>& book) {
            return book->getISBN() == isbn;
        });
    
    if (it != books.end()) {
        // Retire aussi l'ISBN des emprunts pour garder les données cohérentes.
        for (auto& user : users) {
            user->returnBook(isbn);
        }
        books.erase(it);
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}

// Find book by ISBN
Book* Library::findBookByISBN(const string& isbn) {
    auto it = find_if(books.begin(), books.end(),
        [&isbn](const unique_ptr<Book>& book) {
            return book->getISBN() == isbn;
        });
    
    return (it != books.end()) ? it->get() : nullptr;
}

// Search books by title (case-insensitive partial match)
vector<Book*> Library::searchBooksByTitle(const string& title) {
    vector<Book*> results;
    string lowerTitle = title;
    transform(lowerTitle.begin(), lowerTitle.end(), lowerTitle.begin(),
        [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
    
    for (auto& book : books) {
        string bookTitle = book->getTitle();
        transform(bookTitle.begin(), bookTitle.end(), bookTitle.begin(),
            [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
        
        if (bookTitle.find(lowerTitle) != string::npos) {
            results.push_back(book.get());
        }
    }
    return results;
}

// Search books by author (case-insensitive partial match)
vector<Book*> Library::searchBooksByAuthor(const string& author) {
    vector<Book*> results;
    string lowerAuthor = author;
    transform(lowerAuthor.begin(), lowerAuthor.end(), lowerAuthor.begin(),
        [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
    
    for (auto& book : books) {
        string bookAuthor = book->getAuthor();
        transform(bookAuthor.begin(), bookAuthor.end(), bookAuthor.begin(),
            [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
        
        if (bookAuthor.find(lowerAuthor) != string::npos) {
            results.push_back(book.get());
        }
    }
    return results;

12: def plural(count: int, singular: str, plural_form: str) -> str:

17: class MainController:
18:     """Traduit les actions de la vue en opérations sur le modèle."""
19: 
20:     def __init__(
21:         self,
22:         model: Library,
23:         view: MainWindow,
24:         repository: LibraryRepository,
25:     ) -> None:
26:         self.model = model
27:         self.view = view
28:         self.repository = repository
29: 
30:         self._query = ""
31:         self._selected_isbn: str | None = None
32: 
33:         self.view.set_search_callback(self.on_search)
34:         self.view.set_select_callback(self.on_select)
35:         self.view.set_navigation_callback(self.on_navigate)
36:         self.view.set_add_callback(self.on_add_requested)
37:         self.view.set_borrow_callback(self.on_borrow_requested)
38:         self.view.set_delete_callback(self.on_delete_requested)
39: 
40:         self.refresh()
41: 
42:     # Actions déclenchées par la vue
43: 
44:     def on_search(self, query: str) -> None:
45:         """Filtre la liste à partir du champ de recherche."""
46:         if query == self._query:
47:             return
48:         self._query = query
49:         self.refresh()
50: 
51:     def on_select(self, isbn: str) -> None:
52:         """Mémorise le livre sélectionné et adapte les actions."""
53:         if isbn == self._selected_isbn:
54:             return
55:         self._selected_isbn = isbn
56:         self.view.set_selected(isbn)
57:         self._update_selection()
58:         self.view.set_status("")
59: 
60:     def on_navigate(self, section: str) -> None:
61:         """Réapplique les informations de la section Livres."""
62:         if section == "Livres":
63:             self._update_selection()
64: 
65:     def on_add_requested(self) -> None:
66:         self.view.open_add_dialog(self._submit_add)
67: 
68:     def on_borrow_requested(self) -> None:
69:         book = self._selected_book()
70:         if book is None:
71:             return
72: 
73:         if book.available:
74:             if not self.model.users:
75:                 self.view.set_status(
76:                     "Aucun utilisateur enregistré pour un emprunt.", "error"
77:                 )
78:                 return
79:             users = [
80:                 UserRow(user_id=user.user_id, name=user.name)
81:                 for user in self.model.users
82:             ]
83:             self.view.open_borrow_dialog(book.title, users, self._submit_borrow)
84:             return
85: 
86:         self._return_selected(book)
87: 
88:     def on_delete_requested(self) -> None:
89:         book = self._selected_book()
90:         if book is None:
91:             return
92:         if not self.view.confirm_delete(book.title):
93:             return
94: 
95:         try:
96:             self.model.remove_book(book.isbn)
97:         except LibraryError as error:
98:             self.view.set_status(str(error), "error")
99:             return
100: 
101:         self._selected_isbn = None
102:         self.refresh()
103:         if self._save():
104:             self.view.set_status("Livre supprimé.", "success")
105: 
106:     # Soumissions des dialogues
107: 
108:     def _submit_add(self, title: str, author: str, isbn: str) -> str | None:
109:         try:
110:             book = self.model.add_book(title, author, isbn)
111:         except LibraryError as error:
112:             return str(error)
113: 
114:         self._selected_isbn = book.isbn
115:         self._query = ""
116:         self.view.clear_search()
117:         self.refresh()
118:         if self._save():
119:             self.view.set_status("Livre ajouté.", "success")
120:         return None
121: 
122:     def _submit_borrow(self, user_id: str) -> str | None:
123:         book = self._selected_book()
124:         if book is None:
125:             return "Aucun livre sélectionné."
126: 
127:         try:
128:             self.model.borrow(book.isbn, user_id)
129:         except LibraryError as error:
130:             return str(error)
131: 
132:         self.refresh()
133:         if self._save():
134:             self.view.set_status("Livre emprunté.", "success")
135:         return None
136: 
137:     def _return_selected(self, book: Book) -> None:
138:         try:
139:             self.model.return_book(book.isbn)
140:         except LibraryError as error:
141:             self.view.set_status(str(error), "error")
142:             return
143: 
144:         self.refresh()
145:         if self._save():
146:             self.view.set_status("Livre retourné.", "success")
147: 
148:     # Rafraîchissement
149: 
150:     def refresh(self) -> None:
151:         """Reconstruit les lignes affichées et les compteurs."""
152:         if self._selected_isbn is not None and self.model.find_book(
153:             self._selected_isbn
154:         ) is None:
155:             self._selected_isbn = None
156: 
157:         books = self.model.filtered_books(self._query)
158:         visible_isbns = {book.isbn for book in books}
159:         if (
160:             self._selected_isbn is not None
161:             and self._selected_isbn not in visible_isbns
162:         ):
163:             self._selected_isbn = None
164: 
165:         self.view.set_books([self._to_row(book) for book in books])
166:         self.view.set_selected(self._selected_isbn)
167: 
168:         stats = self.model.statistics()
169:         self.view.set_section_subtitle(
170:             f"{plural(stats.total, 'livre', 'livres')} · "
171:             f"{plural(stats.borrowed, 'emprunté', 'empruntés')}"
172:         )
173:         self._update_selection()
174: 
175:     def _update_selection(self) -> None:
176:         book = self._selected_book()
177:         if book is None:
178:             stats = self.model.statistics()
179:             self.view.set_actions(
180:                 can_delete=False,
181:                 can_borrow=False,
182:                 borrow_label="Emprunter",
183:             )
184:             self.view.set_footer_info(
185:                 f"{plural(stats.total, 'livre', 'livres')} · "
186:                 f"{plural(stats.available, 'disponible', 'disponibles')} · "
187:                 f"{plural(stats.borrowed, 'emprunté', 'empruntés')}"
188:             )
189:             return
190: 
191:         self.view.set_actions(
192:             can_delete=True,
193:             can_borrow=(not book.available) or bool(self.model.users),
194:             borrow_label="Emprunter" if book.available else "Retourner",
195:         )
196:         self.view.set_footer_info(self._selection_text(book))
197: 
198:     def _selection_text(self, book: Book) -> str:
199:         if book.available:
200:             return f"Sélection : {book.title} — Disponible"
201: 
202:         borrower = self.model.borrower_name(book)
203:         if borrower:
204:             return f"Sélection : {book.title} — Emprunté par {borrower}"
205:         return f"Sélection : {book.title} — Emprunté"
206: 
207:     @staticmethod
208:     def _to_row(book: Book) -> BookRow:
209:         return BookRow(
210:             isbn=book.isbn,
211:             title=book.title,
212:             author=book.author,
213:             status_label="Disponible" if book.available else "Emprunté",
214:             available=book.available,
215:         )
216: 
217:     def _selected_book(self) -> Book | None:
218:         if self._selected_isbn is None:
219:             return None
220:         return self.model.find_book(self._selected_isbn)
221: 
222:     def _save(self) -> bool:
223:         try:
224:             self.repository.save(self.model)
225:         except OSError:
226:             self.view.set_status(
227:                 "Impossible d'enregistrer les données de la bibliothèque.",
228:                 "error",
229:             )
230:             return False
231:         return True

1: # Interface graphique (Python / customtkinter)
2: 
3: Interface de gestion de la bibliothèque personnelle, construite en MVC avec
4: customtkinter. La mise en page reprend `agent/maquetteUI.png` : barre latérale,
5: en-tête avec recherche, tableau des livres et actions en bas à droite.
6: 
7: Le coeur métier et la persistance sont assurés par le code C++ du projet,
8: exposé à Python avec **pybind11**. La couche Python assure la présentation, la
9: navigation, la validation des saisies et la recherche accent-insensible ;
10: l'état et les opérations de la bibliothèque restent en C++.
11: 
12: ## Prérequis
13: 
14: - Python 3.13 avec Tkinter.
15: - Un compilateur C++17 et CMake (3.21 ou plus).
16: - Un serveur d'affichage X11 ou Wayland. Le devcontainer transmet déjà
17:   `DISPLAY` depuis l'hôte.
18: 
19: ## Installation
20: 
21: ```bash
22: cd agent/UI
23: python3 -m venv .venv
24: .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
25: ```
26: 
27: Le venv est dédié à l'interface et ignoré par Git. Il est distinct du venv
28: utilisé par les notebooks à la racine du dépôt.
29: 
30: ## Compilation du module natif
31: 
32: Le module `bibliotheque_core` doit être compilé avant de lancer l'interface :
33: 
34: ```bash
35: cd agent
36: ./bindings/build.sh
37: ```
38: 
39: Le script utilise le Python de `UI/.venv`, configure CMake avec pybind11 et
40: écrit le module dans `UI/app/`. Il est possible de faire la même chose à la
41: main :
42: 
43: ```bash
44: cd agent
45: cmake -S . -B build-pybind11 \
46:     -DBUILD_PYTHON_BINDINGS=ON \
47:     -DPython_EXECUTABLE="$PWD/UI/.venv/bin/python" \
48:     -Dpybind11_DIR="$("$PWD/UI/.venv/bin/python" -m pybind11 --cmakedir)"
49: cmake --build build-pybind11 --target bibliotheque_core -j
50: ```
51: 
52: Le module compilé est ignoré par Git. Après une modification du C++, relancer
53: `./bindings/build.sh`.
54: 
55: ## Lancement
56: 
57: ```bash
58: cd agent/UI
59: .venv/bin/python main.py
60: ```
61: 
62: Si le module natif est absent, l'application s'arrête avec un message
63: indiquant la commande de compilation à exécuter.
64: 
65: ## Données
66: 
67: L'application lit au démarrage les fichiers du dossier `agent/data/` avec le
68: `FileManager` C++ :
69: 
70: - `books.txt` : `titre|auteur|isbn|disponible|idEmprunteur` ;
71: - `users.txt` : `nom|identifiant|isbn1,isbn2`.
72: 
73: Les actions **Ajouter**, **Emprunter**, **Retourner** et **Supprimer**
74: réécrivent ces deux fichiers au même format que le programme C++. L'écriture
75: se fait dans un fichier temporaire renommé ensuite, afin de ne pas laisser un
76: fichier tronqué en cas d'erreur. Pour revenir aux données d'origine :
77: 
78: ```bash
79: git checkout -- agent/data
80: ```
81: 
82: ## Fonctionnalités
83: 
84: - **Recherche** en direct par titre, auteur ou ISBN, insensible aux accents et
85:   à la casse.
86: - **Tableau** des livres avec statut Disponible / Emprunté, sélection au clic
87:   et mise en évidence de la ligne.
88: - **Ajouter** un livre via une fenêtre modale (validation des champs et
89:   unicité de l'ISBN).
90: - **Emprunter** un livre disponible en choisissant l'utilisateur dans une
91:   liste ; le même bouton devient **Retourner** pour un livre emprunté.
92: - **Supprimer** le livre sélectionné après confirmation.
93: - **Navigation** : Livres est fonctionnel ; Utilisateurs, Emprunts et
94:   Statistiques affichent une section « à venir ».
95: 
96: ## Tests
97: 
98: ```bash
99: cd agent/UI
100: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
101: ```
102: 
103: Les tests qui utilisent le modèle natif sont ignorés avec un message explicite
104: s'il n'a pas été compilé. Le test de fumée de la fenêtre nécessite un affichage
105: et est ignoré automatiquement s'il n'y en a pas :
106: 
107: ```bash
108: xvfb-run -a .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
109: ```
110: 
111: ## Structure MVC
112: 
113: ```text
114: agent/
115: ├── bindings/
116: │   ├── library_bindings.cpp             # module pybind11
117: │   └── build.sh                         # compilation du module
118: ├── book.cpp/h, user.cpp/h
119: ├── library.cpp/h, filemanager.cpp/h     # coeur C++ et persistance
120: └── UI/
121:     ├── main.py                          # composition root
122:     ├── app/
123:     │   ├── config.py                    # dimensions, palette, libellés
124:     │   ├── bibliotheque_core*.so        # module généré, ignoré
125:     │   ├── models/
126:     │   │   ├── book.py                  # dataclass Book
127:     │   │   ├── user.py                  # dataclass User
128:     │   │   └── library.py               # façade Python sur le C++
129:     │   ├── repositories/
130:     │   │   └── library_repository.py    # FileManager C++
131:     │   ├── views/
132:     │   │   ├── main_window.py           # fenêtre, sidebar, en-tête, pied
133:     │   │   ├── book_table.py            # tableau scrollable
134:     │   │   ├── dialogs.py               # ajout et choix d'utilisateur
135:     │   │   └── view_models.py           # BookRow / UserRow
136:     │   └── controllers/
137:     │       └── main_controller.py       # câblage vue ↔ modèle ↔ dépôt
138:     └── tests/
139:         ├── test_bindings.py
140:         ├── test_library.py
141:         ├── test_repository.py
142:         ├── test_controller.py
143:         └── test_view_smoke.py
144: ```
145: 
146: Règles de dépendance :
147: 
148: - l'état des livres et des utilisateurs vit dans le C++ ; la façade Python ne
149:   fait que convertir et valider les entrées ;
150: - la vue n'importe pas le modèle ; elle reçoit des `BookRow` / `UserRow`
151:   prêts à afficher ;
152: - le contrôleur ne crée aucun widget ;
153: - le dépôt centralise les accès aux fichiers via le `FileManager` C++ ;
154: - seul `main.py` connaît les trois couches à la fois.

    def filtered_users(self, query: str = "") -> list[User]:
        """Filtre les utilisateurs par nom ou identifiant, sans accents."""
        query = query.strip()
        if not query:
            return self.users

        needle = normalize(query)
        return [
            user
            for user in self.users
            if needle in normalize(user.name)
            or needle in normalize(user.user_id)
        ]

    def add_user(self, name: str, user_id: str) -> User:
        """Ajoute un utilisateur après validation des champs."""
        name = self._clean_field(name, "Le nom")
        user_id = self._clean_field(user_id, "L'identifiant")

        if self._core.find_user(user_id) is not None:
            raise LibraryError(
                f"Un utilisateur avec l'identifiant {user_id} existe déjà."
            )

        user = self._native.User(name, user_id)
        self._core.add_user(user)
        return self._to_user(user)

def test_user_rows_follow_borrow_and_return() -> None:
    _, view, _, _ = build()
    view.select_callback("9782070612758")

    view.borrow_callback()
    _, _, submit = view.borrow_dialog
    assert submit("USR002") is None

    row = next(row for row in view.users if row.user_id == "USR002")
    assert row.borrowed_count == 1
    assert row.borrowed_titles == "Le Petit Prince"

    view.select_callback("9782070612758")
    view.borrow_callback()

    row = next(row for row in view.users if row.user_id == "USR002")
    assert row.borrowed_count == 0
    assert row.borrowed_titles == ""
```

def test_save_includes_added_user(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    library = Library()
    library.add_user("Sophie Lemaire", "USR003")
    repository = LibraryRepository(tmp_path)

    repository.save(library)

    assert (tmp_path / "users.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == (
        "Sophie Lemaire|USR003|\n"
    )

    reloaded = repository.load()
    assert reloaded.find_user("USR003").name == "Sophie Lemaire"

30: - Persistence formats: `books.txt` = `title|author|isbn|1|borrowerId`; `users.txt` = `name|userId|isbn1,isbn2`. Writes go through a temporary file then a rename, so an error cannot leave a truncated data file.
31: - Python bindings: `./bindings/build.sh` builds the `bibliotheque_core` module with the UI venv. It requires pybind11 (installed by `UI/requirements-dev.txt`). In CMake, the module is optional: `-DBUILD_PYTHON_BINDINGS=ON`; it outputs to `agent/UI/app/`.
32: 
33: ## Python UI (`agent/UI/`)
34: - Dedicated venv: `agent/UI/.venv` (git-ignored). Do not reuse the root notebook venv.
35: - Setup: `cd agent/UI && python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`
36: - Build native module: `cd agent && ./bindings/build.sh`. It uses the UI venv and writes `agent/UI/app/bibliotheque_core*.so` (git-ignored). Re-run it after any C++ change.
37: - Run: `cd agent/UI && .venv/bin/python main.py`. Requires an X display (`DISPLAY` is forwarded by the devcontainer). Without the native module, the app exits with an explicit build instruction.
38: - Tests: `cd agent/UI && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`. Tests that exercise the native model (library, repository, controller) require the module and skip with an explicit message if it is missing; build it first. GUI smoke tests need a display; use `xvfb-run -a` when `DISPLAY` is unset.
39: - MVC layout: `app/models/book.py` and `user.py` are dataclasses; `app/models/library.py` is a thin facade over the pybind11 module, which owns the C++ `Book`/`User`/`Library` state. `app/repositories` uses the C++ `FileManager`; `app/views` contains only CTk widgets and receives `BookRow`/`UserRow`; `app/controllers` wires everything; `main.py` is the composition root.
40: - Bindings source: `agent/bindings/library_bindings.cpp`; CMake target `bibliotheque_core`. Getters return copies to avoid dangling C++ pointers.
41: - Data: `agent/data/books.txt` (`titre|auteur|isbn|1|` or `0|USRxxx`) and `users.txt` (`nom|id|isbn1,isbn2`). The UI reads at launch and rewrites both files atomically after add/borrow/return/delete; restore with `git checkout -- agent/data`.
42: - Screen: sidebar Livres/Utilisateurs/Emprunts/Statistiques (only Livres is active), accent-insensitive search by title/author/ISBN (implemented in Python on the C++ data), book table, and Ajouter / Emprunter↔Retourner / Supprimer.
43: - UI text and comments are French; identifiers are English.
44: 
45: ## Verification
46: - No formatter or linter. C++ has no automated tests; verify it with a clean CMake build (warnings are strict: `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic`). Verify notebook changes by running the affected notebook from its directory with the venv kernel.
47: - Bindings: `cd agent && ./bindings/build.sh`, then import-check with `cd UI && .venv/bin/python -c "from app import bibliotheque_core; print(bibliotheque_core.__doc__)"`.
48: - UI: build the native module first, then from `agent/UI`, run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`, then smoke-launch with `timeout 5 .venv/bin/python main.py` (exit code 124 means the window stayed open).

## Filtre « Disponibles uniquement » (section Livres)

**Interface**
- `books_body` ligne 0 : champ de recherche en colonne 0 (extensible), `CTkCheckBox` **« Disponibles uniquement »** en colonne 1, aligné à droite.
- Styles repris de `config` (text muted, accent pour la coche), case décochée par défaut.
- Callback `set_availability_filter_callback(...)` + méthode interne déclenchée à chaque changement.

**Modèle**
- `filtered_books(query="", available_only=False)` : la condition `book.available` s'ajoute au filtre texte existant.

**Contrôleur**
- État `_available_only`, méthode `on_availability_filter(active)` puis `refresh()`.
- Le livre sélectionné est désélectionné automatiquement s'il sort de la liste filtrée.
- Compteurs globaux inchangés (total · disponibles · empruntés).

**Comportement**
- Emprunter un livre avec le filtre actif → la ligne disparaît (le livre n'est plus disponible).
- Pour retourner un livre emprunté, il faut décocher le filtre : c'est le comportement logique d'un filtre « à prêter », que je documenterai.

**Tests / docs**
- Tests modèle (filtre seul, combiné à la recherche, inactif), contrôleur (bascule, désélection), smoke test de la case.
- Mise à jour de `agent/UI/README.md` et `agent/chatLogs/AGENTS.md`.
- `agent/data` non modifié.

416:     # Mise à jour de l'affichage
417: 
418:     def set_books(self, rows: list[BookRow]) -> None:
419:         self.book_table.set_rows(rows)
420: 
421:     def set_users(self, rows: list[UserRow]) -> None:
422:         self.user_table.set_rows(rows)
423: 
424:     def set_selected(self, isbn: str | None) -> None:
425:         self.book_table.set_selected(isbn)
426: 
427:     def set_actions(
428:         self,
429:         *,
430:         can_delete: bool,
431:         can_borrow: bool,
432:         borrow_label: str,
433:     ) -> None:
434:         self.delete_button.configure(
435:             state="normal" if can_delete else "disabled"
436:         )
437:         self.borrow_button.configure(
438:             state="normal" if can_borrow else "disabled",
439:             text=borrow_label,
440:         )
441: 
442:     def set_footer_info(self, text: str) -> None:
443:         self.info_label.configure(text=text)
444: 
445:     def set_status(self, message: str, level: str = "info") -> None:
446:         self.status_label.configure(
447:             text=message,
448:             text_color=self._status_color(level),
449:         )
450: 
451:     def set_users_status(self, message: str, level: str = "info") -> None:
452:         self.users_status_label.configure(
453:             text=message,
454:             text_color=self._status_color(level),
455:         )
456: 
457:     @staticmethod
458:     def _status_color(level: str) -> str:
459:         colors = {
460:             "success": config.COLOR_SUCCESS,
461:             "error": config.COLOR_DANGER,
462:             "info": config.COLOR_TEXT_MUTED,
463:         }
464:         return colors.get(level, config.COLOR_TEXT_MUTED)
465: 
466:     def set_section_subtitle(self, text: str) -> None:
467:         self._books_subtitle = text
468:         if self._active_section == "Livres":
469:             self.section_subtitle.configure(text=text)
470: 
471:     def set_users_subtitle(self, text: str) -> None:
472:         self._users_subtitle = text
473:         if self._active_section == "Utilisateurs":
474:             self.section_subtitle.configure(text=text)
475: 
476:     def set_users_footer_info(self, text: str) -> None:
477:         self.users_info_label.configure(text=text)
478: 
479:     def set_section(self, section: str) -> None:
480:         self._active_section = section
481:         for name, button in self._nav_buttons.items():
482:             if name == section:
483:                 button.configure(
484:                     fg_color=config.COLOR_ACCENT_SOFT,
485:                     text_color=config.COLOR_ACCENT,
486:                 )
487:             else:
488:                 button.configure(
489:                     fg_color="transparent",
490:                     text_color=config.COLOR_TEXT_MUTED,
491:                 )
492: 
493:         self.section_title.configure(text=section)
494:         if section == "Livres":
495:             self.section_subtitle.configure(text=self._books_subtitle)
496:             self.placeholder_body.grid_remove()
497:             self.users_body.grid_remove()
498:             self.books_body.grid()
499:         elif section == "Utilisateurs":
500:             self.section_subtitle.configure(text=self._users_subtitle)
501:             self.placeholder_body.grid_remove()
502:             self.books_body.grid_remove()
503:             self.users_body.grid()
504:         else:
505:             self.section_subtitle.configure(text="Section à venir")
506:             self.placeholder_label.configure(
507:                 text=f"La section « {section} » sera disponible prochainement."
508:             )
509:             self.books_body.grid_remove()
510:             self.users_body.grid_remove()
511:             self.placeholder_body.grid()
512: 
513:     def clear_search(self) -> None:
514:         self.search_entry.delete(0, "end")
515:         # CTk 5.2 ne réaffiche pas le placeholder tout seul hors focus.
516:         self.search_entry.configure(placeholder_text=config.SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER)
517: 
518:     def clear_user_search(self) -> None:
519:         self.user_search_entry.delete(0, "end")
520:         self.user_search_entry.configure(
521:             placeholder_text=config.USER_SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER
522:         )

536:     def open_borrow_dialog(
537:         self,
538:         book_title: str,
539:         users: list[UserRow],
540:         on_submit: Callable[[str], str | None],
541:     ) -> None:

544:     def confirm_delete(self, title: str) -> bool:
545:         return messagebox.askyesno(
546:             "Supprimer un livre",
547:             f"Supprimer « {title} » de la bibliothèque ?",
548:             parent=self,
549:         )

551:     # Événements internes
552: 
553:     def _on_search_key(self, _event) -> None:
554:         if self._search_callback is not None:
555:             self._search_callback(self.search_entry.get())
556: 
557:     def _on_user_search_key(self, _event) -> None:
558:         if self._user_search_callback is not None:
559:             self._user_search_callback(self.user_search_entry.get())
560: 
561:     def _on_availability_filter_change(self) -> None:
562:         if self._availability_filter_callback is not None:
563:             self._availability_filter_callback(
564:                 bool(self.availability_checkbox.get())
565:             )
566: 
567:     def _on_row_selected(self, isbn: str) -> None:
568:         self.book_table.set_selected(isbn)
569:         if self._select_callback is not None:
570:             self._select_callback(isbn)
571: 
572:     def _on_nav_click(self, section: str) -> None:
573:         self.set_section(section)
574:         if self._navigation_callback is not None:
575:             self._navigation_callback(section)
576: 
577:     def _on_add_click(self) -> None:
578:         if self._add_callback is not None:
579:             self._add_callback()
580: 
581:     def _on_add_user_click(self) -> None:
582:         if self._add_user_callback is not None:

10: class LibraryRepository:

13:     def __init__(self, data_dir: Path | str) -> None:
14:         native = require_native()
15:         self.data_dir = Path(data_dir)
16:         self.books_path = self.data_dir / "books.txt"
17:         self.users_path = self.data_dir / "users.txt"

23:     def load(self) -> Library:

25:         library = Library()

27:         self._file_manager.load_library(library.native)
28:         return library
29: 
30:     def save(self, library: Library) -> None:
31:         """Écrit les deux fichiers de façon atomique via le C++."""
32:         self.data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

38:             ) from error

40:         if not saved:
